title: Member Handbook: Renting More Than One Area and Security Lighting Rental Light
content:
A member may rent any number of lights under **Area and Security Lighting Rental**. Each light is its own rental, billed on one of the member's service accounts; a farm yard, a shop and a church lot may each carry several lights.

## What this means for a member's lights

- **No limit per member.** The cooperative sets no maximum on the number of lights one member may rent in total.
- **One light, one rental.** Every light stands as a separate rental with its own fixture, its own status and its own billing, even where several lights burn on the same premises.
- **Each rental has one billing account.** Every light is billed on one, and only one, of the member's service accounts. Different lights of the same member may be billed on the same service account or on different ones.

## Questions answered

**Does a member who already rents lights have a limit on renting another?**
Not as a member. The number of lights a member already rents, across all of the member's accounts, places no cap on that member.

**Are two lights in the same yard one rental?**
No. Each light is its own rental, billed on one of the member's service accounts, whether it stands alone or beside others.

**May a member with a home meter and a shop meter have lights on each?**
Yes. Each light is billed on one of the member's service accounts, and a member's farm yard, shop or church lot may each carry several.

### Hypothetical illustration

A member holds a Schedule FH Farm and Home Service account for the farm home and a Schedule GS-1 Single-Phase General Service account for a shop. The member rents two lights over the farm yard and one over the shop door. That is three rentals: each light is its own rental, and each is billed on one of the two accounts the member chooses for it.
